carousels.name: 7 things to do with restless hands at night

slides.title: Day 18. Restless hands, nothing to do. [[7 ways to keep them off p*rn tonight.]]
slides.sub: Your hands are bored. Give them a job.

slides.title: Hands busy, [[1–3]] — no p*rn
items: Cook something from scratch — chopping, stirring, plating.
Build or fix something — LEGO, a bike, a shelf.

slides.title: Away from p*rn [[4–5]]
items: Draw or write by hand — paper, not phone.
Play a card or board game with someone.

slides.title: Hands busy [[6–7]]
items: Grip work — a stress ball, hand gripper, kettlebell.
Clean one room — finished task, clear head.

slides.title: Busy hands, [[quiet]] urges.
slides.body: Many p*rn urges start with an idle hand reaching for a phone. Give your hands a job before the urge gives them one.

carousels.name: Should it be No P*rn November instead of No Nut November?

slides.title: Should it be called No P*rn November instead? [[We think yes.]]
slides.sub: Here's why — tell us if you agree.

slides.title: The meme misses the [[point]]
slides.body: NNN focuses on a single act. The habit that actually runs people's lives is p*rn. Quit the right thing.

slides.title: P*rn is the [[engine]]
slides.body: The searching, the scrolling, the late nights, the escalation, the hiding — that's the loop that does the damage.

slides.title: It lasts [[longer]]
slides.body: "No nut" ends Nov 30 for most people. "No p*rn" is something you can keep in December, January and beyond.

slides.title: Our [[take]]
slides.body: Keep the challenge — it gets people started. But make the real goal no p*rn. That's the change that sticks.

carousels.name: The conversation p*rn lets you skip

slides.title: Behind most nights of p*rn is [[a conversation you're dodging.]]
slides.sub: With her. With your boss. With your dad. With yourself.

slides.title: The talk with [[her]]
slides.body: "I feel distant." "I'm not happy with us." "I need more." P*rn is easier than saying it. It also guarantees nothing changes.

slides.title: The talk about [[work]]

One p*rn session buys you an evening of not thinking about it.

carousels.name: 1 in 4 men seeking help for new ED were under 40

slides.title: About 1 in 4 men seeking help for new erection problems [[were under 40.]]
slides.sub: And many young men in recovery link theirs to p*rn.

slides.title: Were [[40 or younger]]
slides.body: At one clinic in Milan, 26% of 439 men seeking help for new erectile dysfunction were 40 or younger (Capogrosso et al., 2013).

slides.title: Young doesn't mean [[immune]]
slides.body: The researchers noted many younger patients had no other health problems. It's more common in young men than most people think.

slides.title: Where p*rn [[fits in]]
slides.body: Many men in recovery forums say their problems with real partners improved after cutting out p*rn. The study didn't measure p*rn — so see a doctor and look at your habits too.

slides.title: If it's [[you]]
items: See a doctor — rule out medical causes first.
Be honest with them about your p*rn use.
Talk to your partner instead of hiding it.
slides.note: Send this to a friend who's too embarrassed to ask ↗

[[without p*rn.]]

slides.title: Your p*rn excuse at 14, 18, 22 and 26. [[Notice anything?]]
slides.sub: The excuse changes. The habit doesn't.

slides.title: "I'm just [[curious]]."
slides.body: Everyone's talking about it. You click once. Nobody tells you how sticky p*rn is.

slides.title: "Everyone [[does it]]."
slides.body: It's daily now. Late nights. Hidden tabs. You tell yourself it's normal.

slides.title: "I'm [[stressed]]."
slides.body: Exams, jobs, rejection. P*rn is the go-to relief. You've tried to stop. It didn't hold.

slides.title: "I'll quit [[when life settles]]."
slides.body: Twelve years in. Same habit, better excuse. Don't let 30 be the next line on this list.
